title: KV handle refcount mismatch and arena fragmentation causing intermittent GPU OOMs across deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported intermittent GPU out-of-memory (OOM) crashes during long-running conversational workloads. Investigation shows a long-tail fragmentation pattern in the runtime tensor/arena allocator combined with a subtle KV-cache handle refcount mismatch that prevented proper eviction/compaction. This manifests as slowly increasing device memory pressure and eventually OOMs under moderate sustained load.

Affected surfaces: hosted API endpoints (sporadic), dedicated GPU pools under high throughput, and private VPC installs where customers had large session lifetimes (>=30m). Notably reproducible in worst-case multi-tenant stress tests and observed in two P1 customer escalations (ticket references linked below).

Root cause hypothesis: A race between the KV-cache eviction path and the session compaction worker could decrement refcounts twice for some KV handles during rapid evict+rebind cycles. Those handles became logically dead but left small, non-contiguous slabs in GPU arena that prevented coalescing. Over time the allocator's free-list fragmentation produced many micro-gaps that the GPU kernel scheduler could not utilize for larger tensors, triggering OOMs.

Why this is different: Prior fixes addressed single causes (e.g., outright leaks or single-threaded compaction). This incident required coordinating fixes in three places: KV handle lifecycle (atomic refcounting), arena coalescer (merge adjacent free slabs aggressively), and a short-term scheduling mitigation to avoid large-kernel placements in fragmented arenas.
updates: 2026-03-10: Incident triage call. Collected heap snapshots from customer A (private) and customer B (dedicated). Identified repeating pattern of small free slabs (~64KB-1MB) and KV handle tombstones in traces.

2026-03-11: Reproducer created: stress-kv-rebind.py (conservative bindings + accelerated eviction) reproduces fragmentation locally at ~45m run. Added to runtime/integration/stress/ folder and test harness. Link in 'links'.

2026-03-11: Patch candidate 1: atomic_refcount_patch (runtime/kv/handle_refcount.cc) implemented. Adds a 64-bit atomic refcount and compares during release to avoid double-free path. Unit tests added.

2026-03-12: Patch candidate 2: arena_coalescer_v2 (runtime/allocator/arena_coalesce.cc) implemented. Coalescer now walks free-list opportunistically on thresholds and merges adjacent free-slabs during low-load cycles. Benchmarked with microbench; shows 12% reduction in fragmentation under synthetic workload.
2026-03-12: Scheduler mitigation: kernel-alloc-hint introduced for large tensor placements to prefer nodes with contiguous spans; enabled behind flag runtime.debug.prefer_contiguous=true for rollout.
2026-03-13: Integration test run with repro harness for 72h (nightly) against dedicated pool. No OOMs observed while both patches active. Memory profiles show plateau vs previous ramp.

2026-03-13: Code review pending for arena_coalescer_v2 (PR link). Security reviewed KV changes; no keys or secrets touched. Performance review scheduled to validate tail latency impact for small models.

2026-03-13: Customer communications prepared: advised temporary mitigations (lower session TTL, reduce burst concurrency, enable preempt flag). Customers on Dedicated rotated to canary build with patches for early verification.

Next steps: merge atomic_refcount_patch (blocked on one unit test race), get arena_coalescer_v2 through perf signoff, rollout to runtime-1.19 canary, monitor 7-day MTBF on canary before full rollout. Postmortem and automation of a fragmentation detection alert are in planned actions.
links: Customer escalation ticket: CUST-4521 (Private deployment), CUST-4582 (Dedicated)
postmortem_actions: Automate fragmentation monitor: add alert when free-slab-count > 10k or contiguous_free_ratio < 0.25 for 10m window.
Add regression test to CI that runs stress-kv-rebind for 1h in pre-merge to catch refcount races.
Backport atomic_refcount_patch to 1.18.x LTS branch and prepare emergency hotfix for Hosted tenant groups.
Document KV lifecycle invariants in runtime dev docs and add pair-programming session for allocator owners.
